text:
**continue**: land CL58. Separately, launch a one-line test fix: `tests/test_resume_attached_boards.py` reads the real `origin/board-mirror` (owner comment `3aec2f488e424ae59968`, 02:51 today) and is red on main and on cl58 for anyone right now.

## Holds
Rerun on branch `cl58` at 7eb5445 (worktree from origin/cl58), in this web session (session id set):
- **check**: `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_cl39_web_multi.py tests/test_resume_delta.py`: 22 passed with the session id set, and 22 passed with it unset.
- **breaks ("revert")**: I put `scripts/kit.py` and `.kit/kit.py` back to `origin/main` and reran CL39's test: `test_resume_has_no_add_repo_line_with_a_session_id` FAILED (1 failed, 9 passed). Restored: 10 passed. The check catches the bug.
- **What he asked** ("Its own test is red on main in any session with a session id"): I ran it as he would, in a session with an id, on `origin/main` (eb9ed5b): `test_resume_has_no_add_repo_line` FAILED. On cl58 it passes. Seen red before, green after.
- **The change itself** (diff read): the orchestrator's delta snapshot now holds four sections (web environment, work not landed, unreached parts, git copy behind) and prints a section whole when its text changes. An old snapshot without sections compares nothing, so the first run after an update shows no false change. One thing to watch: the git-copy line contains a count ("N document(s) here are not in git"), so every local write changes it and it will show in most deltas. That is noise, not a failure.
- **Real project**: the orchestrator's Harmonize run (in `real_project`): resume full, then "nothing new", then after `web-env --id` the delta shows "## Web environment (several repos) / env_01RpTest". That is the case the step is about.
- **recheck, "Whole suite with the session id set: 79 of 79 suites passed, 0 failed"**: rerun with `run_all_tests.py --all --keep-going`: **78 passed, 1 failed** (`tests/test_resume_attached_boards.py`, 2 tests). The same 2 fail on `origin/main`, with or without the session id, so this is not CL58. Cause: the byte-for-byte control test reads the owner's unanswered comments from git's real `origin/board-mirror`, which since 02:51 UTC holds an unanswered owner comment (`board/comments/3aec2f488e424ae59968.json`). The test is not hermetic, so it went red when the board changed, not when the code changed. CL58's 79/79 was probably true when it ran. One other suite (`test_checklist_features`) failed once and passed on its two reruns: a flake.

Not checked: the `land` and `unreached` sections changing in a real delta (only web_env is exercised by a test). In this repo's own clone, `kit.web_env` is off, so `web-env --id` refuses here and only the Harmonize run shows the real case.

## Goal
The `cli` train serves "the orchestrator, from one command, sees what needs it": a delta resume that never says "nothing new" while something actionable changed. The measure here is CL39's own test plus a real Harmonize run with an environment id recorded, which is close to the real thing, not a stand-in. The owner's own example (CL39's test red on main in a session with an id) passes. Taken together: the delta resume (M5) has now hidden a section twice, the web environment here and anything else computed from config rather than posts. CL58 adds a list (`RESUME_SECTIONS`) that every new orchestrator section must join by hand. A new section that is left out will be hidden again, silently. A test that fails when a full-resume `##` heading is neither in `RESUME_SECTIONS` nor on the documented left-out list would close that, but it is not needed to land this. The train card shows state "you" (waiting on the owner). With this partial pull I cannot see when the owner last tried the result himself.

## Verdict
**continue.** Check rerun green with and without an id, break seen failing, the owner's case red on main and green here, and the Harmonize run showing the delta. The one red suite fails identically on main and comes from board data in git, not this change. Suggestion: land it, and have the next part make `test_resume_attached_boards.py` hermetic (stub the owner-comments source the way it already stubs `_resume_extras` and `_resume_queue`), because it is red on main for every session now.
